clue.text: All-round form of I entertainment

definitions.meaning: a sphere, a shape that is round all over
a grand dance held as a social event

explanation.surface: A pastime that offers a bit of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'of I' is an OCR misreading of 'or', which joins the two definitions; 'All-round' looks like versatile but means spherical.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a spherical object and a formal dance party, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: How to conceal a yawn when it's late

definitions.meaning: polite people yawn with a palm over the mouth

explanation.surface: Covering a yawn late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm hides a yawn, and the word also means overdue.

clue.text: He really likes being fifty too!

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
over means excessively, too

explanation.surface: A man who loves being fifty as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adores something is a devotee of it.

clue.text: Having sinister 2 propensities

parts.note: sinister is the heraldic Latin for left, so leaning to the left side, rather than evil leanings

explanation.surface: Someone with a wicked streak.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray 2 is OCR noise. 'Sinister' reads as evil, but in Latin and heraldry it means left.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister originally meant on the left, so a person favouring the left hand has sinister tendencies.

clue.text: Caustic with Oriental pest?

parts.note: E stands for east
a rat or mouse is a vermin pest

explanation.surface: An acid-tongued remark about an Eastern pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A corroding substance wears away, so it is caustic.

clue.text: Staggers the salvage-collectors

definitions.meaning: in British slang, rag-and-bone men who collect scrap

explanation.surface: The scrap collectors are reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, people collecting scrap from the streets were known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeling walkers wobble, and old British slang names scrap gatherers this way.

clue.text: Gathers there's a very large number on dope

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
an ass is a fool, a dope

explanation.surface: A drug-related gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on dope' sounds like drugs; dope is a fool and 'on' puts it after.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate is to collect, a synonym.

clue.text: Spoil a great set-up and this will cause an outburst

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rot is to go bad, spoil
noted means famous or great

explanation.surface: Ruining a big plan will cause an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' turns ROT A NOTED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge triggering a bomb sets off an explosion, an outburst.

clue.text: So sarcastic about duck — and fish

indicators.note: the sarcastic word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: dry humour is wryly sarcastic
O, as a zero score in cricket

explanation.surface: Sneering at a bird and a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O.
explanation.definitionFit: The John Dory is a sea fish.

clue.text: The second-in-command achieved management

indicators.note: management means handling, so the letters of the word are handled into a new order

explanation.surface: The deputy has risen to running the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'management' looks like the definition of HEAD, but it is the anagram signal working on 'achieved'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy leader ranks just below the principal, holding second place in authority.

clue.text: Discuss the dentist's final 4 recommendation

definitions.meaning: to argue a matter through to a conclusion
when filling fails, the dentist advises pulling the tooth

explanation.surface: Talking over what the dentist last advised.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash a dispute out is to argue it openly, and a dentist's last resort is extraction of the tooth.

clue.text: Post back with a certain hesitation

parts.note: aft means at the back of a ship
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Sending a letter back after some dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like mail but is the definition, meaning later, as in post-war.
explanation.definitionFit: Post- as a prefix means later in time, a synonym.

clue.text: European from Aragon or Seville

indicators.note: the letters are taken out from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A Spaniard from one of two Spanish places.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Spain, but the letters span 'aragoN OR SEville' to give a Scandinavian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian of old Norway is a native of a northern part of the continent, so a European.

clue.text: Regular air service

parts.note: even means steady or regular
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A scheduled flight service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular air service' reads like an airline timetable; the service is a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglican evening prayer is a church service.

clue.text: It's always the same when one's out of ready money!

parts.note: coins in the pocket are change
lacking or without, the suffix -less

explanation.surface: A grumble that being broke never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready money' reads as cash in general; here it is small coins, and 'out of' gives the suffix meaning without.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unvarying stays constant, never altering.

clue.text: Spinning threads can be 8 most difficult

indicators.note: the word threads is spun round into a new order, matching the textile picture

explanation.surface: Spinning yarn is the toughest job.
explanation.definitionFit: Toughest, superlative of tough, means most difficult.

clue.text: Someone thinking to show spirit in a rocky situation

parts.note: rum is a spirit
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A drinker reflecting in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who ponders deeply chews things over.

clue.text: Increase of time spent in 9 jail

explanation.surface: A longer prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen is to enlarge, and in criminal slang a term inside is a stretch.

clue.text: Break down or hide, as in a former state

indicators.note: the letters of or hide as are broken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Fall apart or go into hiding in a lost country.
explanation.definitionFit: The old African colony, now Zimbabwe and Zambia, was a state.

clue.text: Unsettled CID man prepared 14 to admit nothing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, or admit, the next piece
the letters of CID man are made ready in a new arrangement

parts.note: O looks like the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A rattled detective has primed himself to confess nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges CIDMAN to NMADIC, and 'to admit' puts O inside it. CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home is unsettled, a synonym.

clue.text: Study travel in outline

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
a tour is a trip

explanation.surface: Researching a trip in sketch form.
explanation.definitionFit: The shape or profile line of a thing is its outline.

clue.text: Source of cash for the Highlander? That depends on him!

definitions.text: Source of cash for the Highlander? That depends on him!

parts.words: Source of cash for the Highlander? That depends on him!
parts.note: a Scot keeps money in the pouch worn at the front of the kilt, which hangs from his belt, so it literally depends on him

explanation.surface: Where a Scot gets his money is up to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depends on' means relies on in the surface, but here it means hangs from. A Highlander is a Scot from the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The kilt pouch is a purse hanging from a Scotsman's belt.

clue.text: Quite out of the ordinary place is crumbling

indicators.note: the letters of place is fall apart and regroup

explanation.surface: An unusual building falling into ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraordinary or exceptional is a synonym.

clue.text: Going in for charm

definitions.meaning: to delight or enchant, stressed on the second syllable

explanation.surface: Entering in order to win people over.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming inside is an arrival, and to enchant is a verb sense with a shifted stress.

clue.text: About a quarter fall — get arrested

indicators.note: the fall of water goes about the quarter

parts.note: rain falls from the sky
N is north, a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Falling a quarter of the way and being caught.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken into custody is in slang to be pulled in by the police.

clue.text: A bore -but sounds 20 keen

indicators.note: the clue says the word for keen is heard, giving another spelling

parts.note: eager means keen

explanation.surface: Someone tedious who seems enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bore' looks like a tedious person; it is a tidal wave running up a river, as on the Severn or Trent in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal surge up an estuary is called a bore.

clue.text: Note value just to be irritating

parts.note: G is a musical note
to rate is to value

explanation.surface: Assessing a musical note just to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rasp on the nerves is to be annoying, a synonym.

clue.text: Suffices for some herbivores

explanation.surface: Some plant-eaters are enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Is enough is a synonym of serves, and female deer graze on plants.

clue.text: Frequently expressed as decimal

definitions.meaning: read as two words, in base ten

explanation.surface: Numbers are usually written in decimal.
explanation.definitionFit: Many times is a synonym, and decimal notation is counting by tens.

clue.text: Start to speak about the single trap

indicators.note: the speaking word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: orate means to speak formally
I is the Roman numeral one
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: Beginning a speech on the lone trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin or arise is a synonym of start.

clue.text: Chinese food that's bound to go round!

parts.note: a spring is a leap or bound
to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: A dish that's sure to spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' reads as certain; it means leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried pancake filled with vegetables is a Chinese dish.

clue.text: Stocking fillers

parts.note: not small Christmas gifts but the limbs that fill hosiery

explanation.surface: Small Christmas presents.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs are what fill hosiery.
